I've run out of time, so here's the complete brief built only from what I actually opened and read. I'm flagging clearly where I could not verify details.

## 1. What media/entertainment employers expect from IT engineers

From the Paramount "Lead IT Engineer, Digital Media & Production Technology Services" posting (Los Angeles, via EntertainmentCareers.Net) and the Company 3 Avid Engineer posting, the requirements that recur are:

**Recurring requirements (the ones I kept seeing):**
1. **Post-production / digital-media workflow expertise** — supporting Avid (Media Composer), Interplay/Production, Media Central, media asset management, editorial pipelines, and digital media processing (e.g., Telestream Vantage, Intera Baton). Paramount: "Minimum 4 years of experience supporting post-production and/or digital media processing workflows."
2. **Cloud + infrastructure engineering** — AWS and/or Azure (lift-and-shift and cloud-native), Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes), storage performance and archival, high-performance NFS/S3 object storage.
3. **Cross-platform systems administration + scripting** — Windows, macOS, Linux; scripting in Linux shell, PowerShell, or Python.
4. **Video/media format standards knowledge** — 1080i/p, 4K, HDR, colorspace, timecode, framerate, codec, PCM, 5.1, Atmos.
5. **Monitoring/observability + cybersecurity** — Zabbix/Splunk/Sumo Logic/New Relic; "knowledge of current cybersecurity standards and best practices."
6. **Client/creative communication** — "Love of interacting with creative professionals, video editors, designers, animators."
7. Education: "A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, though equivalent experience will also be considered."

**Two concrete training/certification routes that fit this space:**
- **Avid ACSR (Avid Certified Support Representative) path** (avid.com): ACSR: Media Composer → ACSR: Avid NEXIS → ACSR: MediaCentral | Production Management → ACSR: MediaCentral | Cloud UX → **ACSR: Elite Video**. It's exam-based (not course-based), and Avid lists it as the credential Paramount explicitly "prefers." Avid describes ACSR for Media Composer as "a technical support certification for engineers and technicians who support and maintain Avid systems."
- **AWS Media Services training/certification** (aws.amazon.com/training): AWS Skill Builder (600+ free courses), "Video Streaming Essentials for AWS Media Services," and a Media Services Ramp-Up Guide aimed at "media engineers, and media operators." This maps directly to the cloud/object-storage requirement.
- (Supporting: a CS/Engineering degree or equivalent, plus general IT sysadmin/VMware/Active Directory.)

## 2. Local 700 (Motion Picture Editors Guild) — West Coast / LA entry

Source: editorsguild.com/Join/Join-West-Coast (left open), plus the guild's New-Member-Initiation-Fee page and csatf.org.

- **Two separate processes:** (a) getting on the **CSATF Industry Experience Roster (IER)**, and (b) **union membership**. "Placement on the Roster does not automatically trigger union membership or vice-versa."
- **Roster first:** "most classifications working in Los Angeles County must be on the CSATF Industry Experience Roster prior to accepting union employment." Required for all classifications **except** Foley Artist and Sound Service Person (Y16).
- **Eligibility / experience:** Work must be "like the work covered by the Local 700 Agreements or Videotape Supplemental Agreement," performed in the **US and/or Puerto Rico**. Documentaries must have been screened at a festival/TV/theater. **Industrial and Educational Films do NOT count.** Subscription VOD "can vary."
- **Proof required:** A letter from a non-union employer on company letterhead (or from the payroll company) **plus** proof of payment (W-2s, 1099s, paystubs, or cancelled checks); payment must be at least California minimum wage.
- **How to apply:** Online through the CSATF portal (thehub.org). **No fees to get on the Roster.**
- **Required safety courses:** A — General Production Safety, HP1, and WVP (Sound classifications also need Course K). CSATF's page also lists "Harassment Prevention Training" as a preliminary course.
- **Orientation:** New Member Orientation Meetings via Zoom (roster application, membership responsibilities, pension & health benefits, meeting organizers/field reps).
- **Fees (joining Local 700):** One-time **initiation + processing fee**, varies by contract; payment plan is "half down and the other half within 6 months." **Engineer classification: $3,800 initiation + $100 processing** (valid until 07/31/2027).
- **Joining timing:** "The Guild encourages prospective members to first secure a union job… you must fulfill your obligation to join Local 700 within 30 days of your date of hire."
- **Day-count by classification:** The guild page has a classification dropdown I could not expand (it's JS-driven), so I could not read the exact **Engineer** day requirement from the official page. For reference, a third-party source (topsheet.io) states **Editors = 175 days** of non-union work in the last 3 years and **Colorists = 100 days** in the last 2 years — but I did not confirm the Engineer-specific number on the guild's own page, so treat it as unverified.
- **Contacts:** Membership — Tracy Pacio (323) 978-1087, Tylene Joye (323) 978-1085, membership@editorsguild.com. CSATF — 2710 Winona Ave, Burbank CA 91504, (818) 565-0550, csatf.org.

**Union vs. training-path comparison (brief):** The roster/union route is experience-gated (you need documented, qualifying, paid post-production work first) and is about *getting hired onto union jobs*; the ACSR/AWS training route is skills-gated and is about *becoming employable* for the IT-engineer roles. They're complementary — training makes you qualified, the roster formalizes your eligibility once you have qualifying work.

## 3. Relevant current job examples

**Job 1 — Disney, "Lead Systems Engineer"** (LIVE — opened in a tab, disneycareers.com)
- **Title:** Lead Systems Engineer (Job ID 10159580)
- **Company:** Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology
- **Location:** Glendale, CA / New York, NY / Seattle, WA (LA pay range $129,300–$173,300)
- **Posted:** 21/09/2026
- **Connection to earlier requirements:** Hybrid infrastructure (on-prem + public cloud), "high performance multiprotocol NFS & S3 object storage systems," VMware, Kubernetes, distributed systems, "IaC, CI/CD," 7+ years systems/infrastructure, Bachelor's in a technical field. This is the cloud/storage/infrastructure side of the media-IT profile.
- **Visa/work authorization:** **No explicit mention** — the posting only contains standard EEO and disability-accommodation language. No "we sponsor" or "must be authorized to work" statement appeared in the text I read.

**Job 2 — Company 3, "Systems Engineer, Sr (Post Production Avid Engineer)"** (opened in a tab, ShowbizJobs)
- **Title:** Systems Engineer, Sr (Post Production Avid Engineer)
- **Company:** Company 3 / Method Inc.
- **Location:** Hollywood, CA (On-Site) — pay $85,000–$120,000
- **Connection to earlier requirements:** This is the closest match to the full media-IT profile: "proficient with Avid Media Composer, Avid NEXIS support (**ACSR preferred, not mandatory**)," creative applications, "storage performance and archival concepts," "Active Directory and VMware," "cloud architecture or administration," networking for remote/in-studio workflows.
- **Visa/work authorization:** **No explicit mention** in the text I read.
- **⚠️ Status caveat:** On ShowbizJobs this listing is marked **EXPIRED / filled (closed 07/17/2026)**. I'm including it because it's the most on-point requirements template, but it is **not** a currently open posting. I did not find a second *open* posting I could open in a separate tab before running out of time.

**Additional lead found in search (not opened in its own tab):** Warner Bros. Discovery — "Post Production Engineer," **Burbank, CA** — "lead the post-production technology ecosystem… manage enterprise storage, editing, virtualization, automation and workflows." I saw this in search results but did not open it, so I can't confirm its current status or visa language.

## 4. Rosie O'Donnell / Donald Trump feud timeline

**I did not complete this section.** I ran out of time before researching it, and I did not open or read any source on it. Per my standard of not reporting unverified facts, I will **not** list any dates or events here rather than invent them. If you'd like, I can do that as a follow-up and build the dated timeline from public sources.

## Pages I left open for you
- **editorsguild.com/Join/Join-West-Coast** — the most useful Local 700 page (steps, roster, fees, experience, contacts).
- **disneycareers.com — Disney "Lead Systems Engineer"** (live, full JD with pay range).
- **ShowbizJobs — Company 3 "Systems Engineer, Sr (Post Production Avid Engineer)"** (full JD, but marked expired).
- A DuckDuckGo search results page (post-production engineer jobs) and a blocked ZipRecruiter/Cloudflare page are also still open.

**Honest limitations to note:** (1) The exact **Engineer** day-count for the Local 700 roster is behind a JS dropdown I couldn't expand, so I only have third-party figures for Editor/Colorist as reference. (2) I could only confirm **one** fully-live job posting (Disney); the Company 3 match is expired. (3) The Rosie O'Donnell timeline was not done. Want me to (a) pull the Engineer-specific roster day requirement and (b) complete the Rosie O'Donnell timeline next?
